pages.wrong_reason: The migrated text is the definition of coAM as the complement class of AM (L is in coAM iff its complement is in AM), not a theorem that AM = coAM. The page's own migration note already says the source is definitional (complementation) and that a distinct 'complement-of' edge type is wanted. Do not record an equivalence edge.

sources.ref_file_title: Gro16 - On the Size of Pairing-based Non-interactive Arguments
FKL18 - The Algebraic Group Model and its Applications
sources.authors: Georg Fuchsbauer, Eike Kiltz, Julian Loss
sources.note: Reference page already exists (cryptobib C:FucKilLos18, pp. 33-62). Section on Groth's SNARK proves knowledge soundness in the algebraic group model under the q-discrete-logarithm assumption.

pages.class_justification: Gro16 proves knowledge soundness by a statistical argument against generic adversaries; no computational hypothesis is reduced to, so the RTV04 black-box axis between primitives does not apply. `free` scoped by `model: generic-group` follows the schema's generic-group guidance and the sibling pages red-bilinear-pairing-to-snark-gro16 and red-kea-to-snark-gro16 (both class free, model generic-group).
pages.model_justification: Gro16 proves knowledge soundness in the generic asymmetric bilinear group model. The circuit-specific structured reference string (previously recorded as `crs`) is part of a preprocessing SNARK's syntax and is stated in the statement text; the single model slot carries the idealized proof model.
pages.statement: Arithmetic-circuit satisfiability arithmetized as a [[arithmetization|QAP]] yields the Groth16 preprocessing [[succinct-argument#zk-snark|zk-SNARK]]: under a circuit-specific structured reference string, a proof is $3$ group elements and verification is one pairing-product equation. Zero-knowledge is perfect; knowledge soundness is proved in the generic bilinear group model — [[Gro16 - On the Size of Pairing-based Non-interactive Arguments|Gro16]].
pages.sketch: The reference string encodes powers of a secret point $\tau$ and the trapdoor $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ in the exponent. The prover evaluates the witness's linear combinations of the QAP polynomials at $\tau$ in the exponent to obtain $A$ and $B$, folding the quotient $h(\tau)t(\tau)$ into $C$; the pairing-product equation checks the QAP divisibility relation at $\tau$. A generic adversary can only output linear combinations of reference-string elements, and the verification equation forces those coefficients to encode a valid witness.
pages.improvements_text: - Knowledge soundness of Groth16 in the algebraic group model under the $q$-discrete-logarithm assumption — [[FKL18 - The Algebraic Group Model and its Applications|FKL18]]

sources.ref_file_title: BBHR18 - Scalable, transparent, and post-quantum secure computational integrity
sources.authors: Eli Ben-Sasson, Iddo Bentov, Yinon Horesh, Michael Riabzev
sources.note: Bibliographic data verified against cryptobib EPRINT:BBHR18; reference page exists.

pages.class_justification: AIR and FRI are information-theoretic ingredients and the random-oracle compilation reduces to no computational primitive, so the RTV04 axis between primitives does not apply. The repo scopes `free` by an idealized model only for generic-group edges (schema/reduction-classes.yaml prescribes `class: free` for `generic-group` but only 'pick a class' for `rom`, and every existing `model: rom` reduction is `unstated`), so no class is recorded.
pages.model_justification: BBHR18 compile the STARK interactive oracle proof to a non-interactive argument by Merkle-hashing the oracles and applying Fiat–Shamir, analysed with the hash as a random oracle. The migration recorded rom as an inference; the source confirms it.
pages.statement: A computation expressed as an [[arithmetization|AIR]], with the constraints checked by the [[polynomial-commitment#fri-fast-reed-solomon-iop-of-proximity|FRI]] proximity test, yields the STARK of BBHR18: a transparent [[succinct-argument|succinct argument]] of knowledge with no trusted setup, prover time quasi-linear and verification time and proof length polylogarithmic in the computation size $T$, made non-interactive in the random-oracle model — [[BBHR18 - Scalable, transparent, and post-quantum secure computational integrity|BBHR18]].
pages.sketch: The prover Merkle-commits to Reed–Solomon codewords of the execution-trace polynomials; the AIR constraints reduce to a low-degree proximity claim about a derived codeword, which FRI certifies in logarithmically many degree-halving rounds; Fiat–Shamir over the transcript makes the interactive oracle proof non-interactive in the random-oracle model.
notes_to_keep: Genuinely conjunctive ({AIR, FRI} => STARK) — must not be flattened into two single-hypothesis edges.
flags: Both hypotheses are technique/protocol nodes (a Glossary entry and a section of polynomial-commitment), not primitives; class left unstated (see class_justification).

BBHR18's post-quantum claim rests on the interactive STARK using only a collision-resistant hash; the random-oracle analysis recorded here is classical. Quantum-ROM security of the Fiat–Shamir/BCS compilation is later work and is not recorded here.
Conclusion node succinct-argument cannot distinguish transparent STARKs from trusted-setup SNARKs (already noted in migration).
Exact asymptotics (O(T log T) prover, O(log^2 T) proof) could not be checked against the paper in this session (eprint blocked); the statement records only quasi-linear / polylogarithmic.

sources.ref_file_title: BFS20 - Transparent SNARKs from DARK Compilers
sources.authors: Benedikt Bünz, Ben Fisch, Alan Szepieniec
sources.note: Concurrent, independent formalization of polynomial IOPs and their compilation with any polynomial commitment; transparent instantiation from groups of unknown order. Verified: cryptobib EC:BunFisSze20 (Eurocrypt 2020, pp. 677-706, DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-45721-1_24), eprint 2019/1229.

pages.class_justification: The compiler uses the polynomial commitment scheme's algorithms as black boxes, but knowledge soundness routes through the commitment's extractor, whose black-boxness depends on the instantiation (KZG extraction is proved in the AGM); no source classifies the compiled reduction in RTV04 terms.
pages.model_justification: The compiled SNARK is non-interactive via Fiat–Shamir; CHM+20 prove the compiled argument in the random-oracle model. The KZG instantiation additionally needs a universal updatable structured reference string (the previously recorded crs); one model slot cannot carry both, so the SRS is stated in the statement text.
pages.statement: A polynomial IOP for an [[arithmetization|arithmetized]] relation (R1CS, PLONKish), compiled with an extractable [[polynomial-commitment|polynomial commitment scheme]] and made non-interactive by Fiat–Shamir, is a preprocessing [[succinct-argument|SNARK]] in the random-oracle model. Instantiated with [[KZG10 - Constant-size commitments to polynomials and their applications|KZG]] commitments, the structured reference string is universal and updatable; Marlin and Plonk are instances — [[CHM+20 - Marlin Preprocessing zkSNARKs with Universal and Updatable SRS|CHM+20]].
pages.sketch: The polynomial IOP verifier queries the prover's polynomials at random points; each oracle becomes a polynomial commitment and each query an evaluation proof, and Fiat–Shamir removes the interaction. Extractability of the commitment turns the IOP's soundness into knowledge soundness of the argument.

sources.ref_file_title: Wat11 - Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Encryption from Subset Cover
sources.note: Extends the DBDH edge to ciphertext-policy ABE. Three standard-model constructions for monotone formulas, under decisional q-parallel BDHE, decisional BDHE, and DBDH respectively (cryptobib PKC:Waters11, LNCS 6571 pp. 53-70). The reference file's name is wrong (actual title: 'Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Encryption: An Expressive, Efficient, and Provably Secure Realization'); filenames are live URLs, so keep the link.

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction in the bilinear group and one fixed selective-security reduction that embeds the DBDH challenge in the public parameters and challenge ciphertext, answers key queries using the committed target attribute set, and runs the ABE adversary once as an oracle. With an assumption as hypothesis, black-boxness refers to the treatment of the adversary; the proof has the standard fully-black-box shape.
pages.model_justification: GPSW06's selective-security proof for the small-universe construction is in the standard model.
pages.statement: If decisional bilinear Diffie–Hellman ([[bilinear-map-assumptions|DBDH]]) holds, there is a key-policy [[attribute-based-encryption|ABE]] for monotone access structures (monotone Boolean formulas or LSSS) with selective IND-CPA security — [[GPSW06 - Attribute-Based Encryption for Fine-Grained Access Control of Encrypted Data|GPSW06]].
pages.sketch: $\Setup$ publishes $e(g,g)^y$ and per-attribute elements $T_i = g^{t_i}$; a key for an access structure secret-shares $y$ over its leaves, and a ciphertext for attribute set $\gamma$ blinds the message by $e(g,g)^{ys}$ alongside $T_i^s$ for $i \in \gamma$. The selective reduction embeds a DBDH challenge $(g^a, g^b, g^c, Z)$ as $y = ab$, $s = c$, simulates keys for structures unsatisfied by the committed $\gamma^*$, and outputs the adversary's guess as its decision on $Z = e(g,g)^{abc}$.
pages.improvements_text: - Ciphertext-policy ABE for monotone formulas with ciphertext size linear in the formula, selectively secure in the standard model; the most efficient construction is under decisional $q$-parallel BDHE, a less efficient one under DBDH — [[Wat11 - Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Encryption from Subset Cover|Wat11]]
